composing_text: The two Army divisions Harmon designated for the corps (Miller, chapter IX). Marine ground forces already on the island are described in the same chapter; the Marine division headquarters landed two days later.
source_locator: R2225: ch. IX; R2227: Part VI, ch. 9
notes: General Harmon activated or designated the Guadalcanal-Tulagi command as XIV Corps on 2 January 1943; Patch became corps commander and Brigadier General Sebree succeeded him at Americal (Miller, ch. IX; Hough, Ludwig and Shaw, Part VI, ch. 9; CMH chronology of 2 January). Confidence 0.7. This claim file promotes the existing placeholder US-COR-014C; no new corps id was invented.

location_qualifier: Galloping Horse and the inland hills
source_locator: R2225: ch. XI, The 25th Division's Preparations
current_activity: opening the first January offensive west of the Matanikau
notes: Miller, ch. XI: XIV Corps attacked at 0635 on 10 January 1943. The 25th Division, with attachments, was to seize a line about 3,000 yards west of Mount Austen; the 27th Infantry attacked the Galloping Horse and the 35th Infantry the Sea Horse and the Gifu. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment. Existing C12792 and C12817 already record the 25th Division and 27th Infantry attacks that morning.

location_qualifier: coastal and inland approaches to Kokumbona
source_locator: R2225: ch. XIV, Plans and Preparations
current_activity: opening the second January offensive toward Kokumbona
notes: Miller, ch. XIV: Field Order No. 1 of 16 January 1943 ordered XIV Corps to attack west toward a line beyond Point Cruz and the Galloping Horse. The two-division attack was delayed until 22 January for the Hill 66 supply road. That day the 25th Division attacked inland and the CAM Division (2nd Marine Division with the 6th Marines and the 182nd and 147th Infantry) attacked on the coast. Confidence 0.5: Miller only in this increment.

source_locator: R2225: ch. XV, Final Operations on Guadalcanal; R2226: ch. IX, The Final Drive
current_activity: joining the north-coast and south-coast forces at Tenaro, ending organised fighting
notes: Miller, ch. XV, and Zimmerman, ch. IX, agree that the pincer closed on 9 February 1943, ending organised fighting on Guadalcanal. Miller quotes Patch's message to Halsey that total and complete defeat of Japanese forces on Guadalcanal was effected at 1625 that day. Confidence 0.7.
